```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`DSEMr` provides a unified R and compiled Rust framework for Bayesian dynamic
structural equation modeling (DSEM; Asparouhov, Hamaker, & Muthen, 2018),
covering single-level VAR/RDSEM, Tobit censored and probit dynamic models,
two-level location-scale and multivariate DSEM, three-level DSEM (`DSEM3`),
cross-classified DSEM, dynamic factor/IRT models, and penalized shrinkage
priors (`PSEM`).

## Single-level AR(1) and diagnostics

```{r}
library(DSEMr)
dat <- simulate_dsem(n = 100, intercept = 0.2, ar = 0.5, sigma = 0.8, seed = 10)
model <- dsem_model("y ~ lag(y, 1)", time = "time")
fit <- dsem(model, dat, chains = 2, iter = 300, warmup = 150, seed = 10)

summary(fit, standardized = TRUE)
dsem_dic(fit)
```

## Covariate collinearity (VIF) and irregular time intervals (`TINTERVAL`)

Collinearity diagnostics and irregular time-grid alignment are available directly in R:

```{r}
set.seed(11)
dat$x1 <- rnorm(nrow(dat))
dat$x2 <- 0.5 * dat$x1 + rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = 0.85)
m_cov <- dsem_model("y ~ lag(y, 1) + x1 + x2", time = "time")
dsem_vif(m_cov, data = dat)

irregular <- data.frame(time = c(0, 1.05, 3.1, 4.0), y = c(0.2, 0.6, -0.3, 0.1))
dsem_tinterval(irregular, time = "time", delta = 1)
```
